selected_leaf: Derive and falsify the minimal target-side contract required to close the crash-after-effect-before-commit window after the Stage U checkpoint-before-effect barrier, separating idempotent replay/correlation, authoritative committed-effect visibility, and effect-relative negative closure/coverage.

preserved_prior_findings.stage_u_checkpoint_before_effect: A single canonical role-local STATE file updated by file-blob CAS and exact-read back can enforce PREPARED-before-effect ordering for one authorized transition. Repository CAS alone does not close the crash-after-effect-before-matching-commit-witness window for an arbitrary external side effect.

bounded_leaf_result.tested_scope: Target-independent case analysis for one logical_effect_id after a durable PREPARED checkpoint has been exact-read back. No concrete external target or external mutation was invoked. The test classifies which combinations of three target capabilities are sufficient for duplicate-safe retry plus positive completion certification; it does not claim any real target currently provides them.

capabilities.A_idempotent_replay_correlation: A repeated attempt carrying the same logical_effect_id is correlated to the same logical operation and cannot create a second logical effect.
capabilities.B_authoritative_committed_effect_visibil: There is an authoritative positive witness, bound to the logical_effect_id, that can certify the effect committed.
capabilities.C_effect_relative_negative_closure: There is an authoritative negative/closure witness, relative to the same logical_effect_id, after which a prior ambiguous attempt cannot later emerge as committed.

derived_minimal_contract.interpretation: B is semantically indispensable for certifying positive completion unless an idempotent replay response itself supplies the equivalent authoritative committed-result witness. After an ambiguous effect attempt, safe progress requires either A so the same logical effect may be retried without duplicate logical effects, or C so a non-idempotent retry occurs only after authoritative negative closure rules out a late commit from the prior attempt.
derived_minimal_contract.route_A_plus_B: Sufficient for duplicate-safe retries and positive completion certification. C is not required for safety of same-key retry. A terminal negative-failure conclusion remains unresolved unless the replay contract itself supplies a definitive noncommit/terminal result, which is C-equivalent for that decision.
derived_minimal_contract.route_B_plus_C: Sufficient without A if C is strong enough to rule out hidden/in-flight late commit before any retry. Retry may then be issued only after negative closure; a positive B witness ends the logical operation.
derived_minimal_contract.correlation_requirement: Every A, B, or C observation used by the protocol must be bound to the same logical_effect_id; uncorrelated target state is UNKNOWN and mutation-free.

falsification_matrix.reason: Retries can be duplicate-safe, but no authoritative positive witness proves the logical effect committed.

falsification_matrix.result: fails safe-retry liveness after ambiguous outcome
falsification_matrix.reason: A positive witness can certify success, but absence of B is not a safe negative; without A or C an ambiguous attempt cannot be retried mutatively.
Negative closure can authorize a retry after confirmed noncommit, but there is no authoritative positive witness for a committed effect.

falsification_matrix.result: fails positive completion certification unless replay itself yields a B-equivalent committed-result witness
falsification_matrix.reason: Duplicate-safe retry and negative closure do not by themselves prove that a committed effect occurred.

falsification_matrix.result: passes duplicate-safe retry plus positive completion path
falsification_matrix.reason: Same-key retries cannot create duplicate logical effects and B can certify the eventual positive commit; terminal negative-failure certification is not established unless A's replay semantics provide C-equivalent terminal noncommit.

falsification_matrix.result: passes if C is final with respect to late commit
falsification_matrix.reason: No retry occurs while outcome is ambiguous; C first proves the prior attempt cannot later commit, then a new attempt may be issued, while B certifies positive completion.

bounded_leaf_result.unknown_mutation_rule: After an ambiguous effect attempt, UNKNOWN permits only read-only observation. Mutation is authorized only by route A (same logical_effect_id replay under true idempotency/correlation) or after route C has authoritatively closed the prior attempt as noncommitted. Missing/uncorrelated/stale visibility never authorizes a new logical mutation.
bounded_leaf_result.direct_architecture_contribution: Stage U plus Stage V yields a two-part Chat-native safety architecture: repository file-CAS/readback supplies the pre-effect durability barrier; the remaining cross-system contract is narrowed to authoritative positive commit visibility plus either idempotent same-key replay or authoritative negative closure before retry. This removes generic 'external atomicity' as a requirement while preserving the unresolved status of targets that lack the minimal contract.

provenance.semantic_source: own predecessor STATE plus deterministic target-capability case analysis; no public, O, downstream, other-worker, legacy, or shared-ledger semantic input

contradictions: If a target advertised as A can create two logical effects for the same logical_effect_id, route A+B is falsified.
If a target advertised as C can report negative closure and later surface a commit from the closed prior attempt, route B+C is falsified.
If a B witness is not authoritatively bound to the same logical_effect_id, it cannot certify completion for this protocol.
If replay or retry is performed while outcome is UNKNOWN without A or prior C closure, the mutation-safety invariant is violated.
